newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RFM expects 1996 net of 500-550 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: RFM expects 1996 net of 500-550 mln pesos.

text.p: RFM Corp chairman Jose Concepcion said on Tuesday the firm expected a net income of 500 million to 550 million pesos in 1996 due to an upsurge in sales during the fourth quarter.
The projected net income for 1996 is lower than the 1995 figure of 620.6 million pesos.
RFM, one of the Philippines' largest food and beverage companies, had been hurt by high raw material costs.

On Tuesday, it reported a 17 percent fall on unaudited net income for the first nine months to 346.8 million pesos from 419.5 million a year-ago period. The decline, however, was less than the 28 percent slide experienced in the first half.
This was because of improving profits arising from the softening of raw material prices such as sugar, corn, wheat and milk, Concepcion said in a statement.
Moreover, "the oversupply in chicken during the period has put pressure on our bottomline but we are expecting to stabilise in early 1997," he said.
The first half figures of RFM had already prompted analysts to downscale their 1996 profit estimate to a range of between 500 million and 600 million pesos from an earlier 700 million.
Raul Ruiz, vice president of Sun Hung Kai Securities, said he expects RFM to post a 1996 profit of 554 million pesos.
"It's a buy for recovery in 1997," he said.
RFM stock is currently trading at 12.3 times its 1996 estimate earnings per share of 35 centavos, a discount to the market's 19 times.
Ruiz said he expects RFM to post a 25 percent growth in net profits in 1997 due to the rebound of its chicken and meat processing unit, Swift Foods Inc, and lower raw material costs.
The strong sales of Cosmos Bottling Corp and its property unit would also boost profits, he said.
